history.digest:
The Fed's hold at 3.75-4% with SEP dots at 4.25% through 2027 confirmed a higher-for-longer plateau, prompting dealers to trim near-term cut bets toward the dots. Treasury's November 4 refunding statement kept coupon sizes unchanged, capping duration supply and letting intermediate steepeners partially unwind; the 10-year eased a few basis points from its partial-month highs. The CBO's deficit reminder and Powell's framing of term-premium-driven long yields kept fiscal-supply pressure alive, limiting any rally. Net: a slightly flatter, marginally lower long end with term premium still near 1%.
Moves:
- Congressional Budget Office: Issue a public statement or warning: "CBO reminds market participants that its February 2026 baseline incorporates the 2025 reconciliation act (+$4.7 trillion in deficits over 2026-2035), tariffs (-$3.0 trillion), and immigration actions (+$0.5 trillion), projecting a FY2026 deficit of $1.9 trillion (5.8% of GDP) and debt rising to 120% of GDP by 2036. Under current law, CBO's baseline assumes the 10-year Treasury yield rises gradually through 2027 and remains relatively stable thereafter; CBO does not forecast or comment on market yields, term premiums, or market fluctuations. Full details: cbo.gov/publication/62105."
- Federal Reserve / FOMC: Issue a public statement or warning: "Following the September 16 decision to raise the federal funds target range to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, the Committee is maintaining that range. SEP medians hold the funds rate at 4.25 percent at end-2026 and end-2027 while core PCE inflation of 3.4 percent this year remains well above our 2 percent objective; policy will stay sufficiently restrictive, and any adjustment will depend on incoming data on inflation and labor market conditions. The Desk will continue reserve-management purchases of shorter-term Treasuries to maintain ample reserves."
- Jerome Powell (or successor Chair): Issue a public statement or warning (→ Federal Reserve / FOMC, US Department of the Treasury, Primary dealers and Treasury market hedge funds): "Inflation expectations remain well anchored near 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, and the recent rise in longer-term yields reflects higher real yields and term premium rather than a loss of confidence in our framework. With core inflation still elevated, we will maintain a restrictive policy stance and continue to make decisions meeting by meeting, dependent on the data."
